content.title: About
content.content: The Bacon Biscuit Sandwich is a layered sandwich made of a soft biscuit, crispy bacon, lettuce, tomato, and sauce. It combines the sweetness of the biscuit with the salty aroma of bacon, creating a balanced flavor popular in fast‑food and café menus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Bacon Biscuit Sandwich originated in the United States in the early 2000s as an experimental item in fast‑food chains.
Crispy bacon is often achieved by double‑frying the strips.
The biscuit used is typically unsweetened to let the bacon flavor shine.
The sandwich is commonly served with potato wedges or coleslaw.
Variations include adding cheddar cheese, avocado, or a fried egg.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Bacon provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Bacon contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Bacon supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the biscuit and fats from the bacon offers a quick energy boost.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc in bacon supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bacon is often heavily salted, which can raise blood pressure when consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: A large amount of saturated fat may contribute to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The biscuit typically contains wheat flour; those with celiac disease should choose a gluten‑free version.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich is relatively high in calories, so portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Nitrites in bacon
items.content: Some bacon varieties contain nitrites, which can form potentially harmful compounds when overcooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich hot, cut in half. It can be enhanced with mayo or mustard, sliced avocado, cheese, or a fried egg according to personal taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich should be refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours. Keep bacon in an airtight container and store the biscuit in a dry place to prevent sogginess.
